title: How do you get commercial-level game aesthetics with Codex?
author: MarcoSalernoDevelop
selftext:
Hi guys, I've been a programmer for more than 20 years. I started when I was a child and always wanted to make my own videogames.

I was always held back by having zero skills or patience for graphics, modeling, and so on, but I have a strong technical background and a lot of ideas.

I wanted to try making my cool games with AI. I have a Codex Plus subscription and wanted to give it a try, so I set up an environment with Codex, Astra on High mode, Blender, and Godot.

My aim was to be just the art director and let AI do most of the hard work.

Unfortunately, I've only managed to get very low-quality assets, even after having ChatGPT create the prompts, MD files, and project setup for me.

What am I doing wrong? I see a lot of beautiful results from people using the same setup.

Can someone explain how you're achieving such good results? I see a lot of you saying you're not even using any base assets, but idk, it feels like my Astra is much more stupid (and yes, my prompts probably are too, but still...).

PS: I know the Plus subscription doesn't let me do super-long runs. I just wanted to start testing things by making small parts one by one, staying within the given usage limits.

comments.author: thezerg505000
comments.body: There is currently no fast way for generating good models through AI unless you want to use countless tokens and time iterating on models

comments.author: CRNGDNTTLRNT
comments.body:
from my experience working with AI i realized it always needs a reference to go off of
try giving it a good model and tell it to make it in the colors # # and #
then note your adjustments to make a unique model
honestly youd wanna understand management
without that managing AI is gonna be hard and inefficient

replies.author: CRNGDNTTLRNT
replies.body:
i'd recommend learning the basics of management
it's useful for future work with AI since it's gonna be implemented everywhere
and also for working with people
i have a little experience in a management role and figuring out AI was easier for me than for some people i know
